name: Citizenship by Naturalisation (Standard Route)

requirements.blocker_text: At least 5 years of permanent residence (thường trú) in Vietnam up to the time of application, per Article 19 of the Law on Vietnamese Nationality.
requirements.fix_path: Accumulate 5 years of permanent residence in Vietnam.

requirements.blocker_text: Sufficient knowledge of Vietnamese to integrate into the Vietnamese community.
Demonstrated capacity to ensure one's living in Vietnam.

Must renounce foreign nationality upon naturalising, except in special cases approved by the President of Vietnam (see vn_citizenship_relaxed_naturalisation.json for the categories now exempted by the 2025 amendment).

evidence_required.document: Proof of 5 years' permanent residence in Vietnam
Proof of financial capacity to sustain living in Vietnam
Written renunciation of foreign nationality (unless exempted)

sources.title: Government Portal (chinhphu.vn) -- Law No. 24/2008/QH12 on Vietnamese Nationality, Article 19: naturalisation conditions (5 years' permanent residence, Vietnamese language sufficiency, capacity to sustain living in Vietnam, renunciation of foreign nationality except special Presidentially-approved cases)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Vietnam). dual_citizenship_allowed is false for THIS standard route since renunciation is the general rule under Article 19 -- but see vn_citizenship_relaxed_naturalisation.json for the 2025-amended track (spouses/children/descendants of Vietnamese citizens, or those with special contributions) which both waives the residence/language/means tests AND permits retaining foreign nationality; that amendment (Law effective 1 July 2025, reported via Nhan Dan, Vietnam's official Communist Party newspaper, treated as tier-2 rather than tier-1 since it is not the legally-designated Gazette) does not appear to have changed THIS standard route's core figures -- a tier-2 source explicitly states the 5-year residence requirement 'remains' unchanged for standard cases, consistent with the tier-1 Article 19 text quoted here, so this file is published without a live-transition caveat (contrast with Peru's Ley 32421 naturalisation file, which IS held draft over a genuine unresolved dispute about which rule currently applies).
